chunks: By this chain of narration, he said: Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) would say:

Act with deliberation, for surely you will die. And choose for yourself, O human being, for it is as though what has already occurred never happened once it has passed, and as though what is yet to come has already been.

key_terms.كائن: Ka'in — that which is coming into being; the present and near future
key_terms.مهل: Mahal — deliberation, steadiness; acting thoughtfully without haste

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the transience of life and preparing for death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) frequently recited these poetic verses urging people to act thoughtfully while they still can. The poem reminds the listener that life is fleeting: the past vanishes as if it never happened, and the future will soon become the past. In the original context, this was an exhortation to prepare for the afterlife by choosing good deeds while alive, since death is inevitable and time is illusory.
